title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering under regional failover + load-shedding
author: Priya Raman
description:
Context: We observed production incidents during a regional outage + subsequent load-shedding event where the SLO enforcer's backoff ordering and hysteresis logic caused cascading drops in capacity and unnecessary full-region failovers. Root cause was a race between the async backoff queue reconciliation and the regional failover path: backoffs were being applied out-of-order when simultaneous updates arrived from the replication stream, causing premature circuit tripping and aggressive load-shedding.

What this PR does: Hotfix to stabilize SLO enforcer ordering and backoff hysteresis: 1) serialize backoff updates per-route using a lightweight per-route epoch counter to ensure ordering across async streams; 2) add guarded hysteresis window (configurable) to prevent re-tripping within short time windows during regional failover; 3) tighten metrics and tracing to make ordering/delay visible for future incidents; 4) add more defensive nil-checks in regional failover path to avoid double-apply during rapid leader elections.

Testing & verification: unit tests for ordering logic and hysteresis; stress-test in perf-canary with synthetic failovers reproducing the race; manual canary rollout to a single region for 2 hours under simulated load-shedding, validated by SLO dashboards (token latency p50/p95 unaffected, error budget burn improved).

Rollback & deployment notes: This is a small hotfix that touches the enforcer core and the regional failover orchestration. Deploy with gradual canary: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 45 minutes. If SLO enforcer metrics show >2x baseline re-trips or regional-failover-count increases, rollback to previous main and alert SRE.

Motivation: Prior incidents (SUP-8765) caused customer-facing latency spikes and unnecessary capacity churn. This change reduces the likelihood of ordering-induced failovers and makes load-shedding decisions more conservative when regional elections are in-flight.

Checklist: [x] Repro case added to perf-canary harness; [x] Unit tests; [x] Integration stress-run; [x] Metrics+traces added; [x] Reviewed & approved by SRE and runtime ownership.

Notes: change is non-breaking; configuration knobs added are defaulted to safe values but are documented in infra/README for operators.

review_comments: Ethan Park (reviewer): Can you explain how the epoch counter is persisted across restarts? Is it safe for leader handoffs?

Priya Raman (author): The epoch counter is in-memory with a short-lived monotonic counter per-route; leader handoff reconciles by using stream sequence numbers as a safe upper-bound and rehydrates epoch from last-applied stream position - added comment in enforcer.go explaining this and a fallback to conservative ordering on ambiguity.
Maria Gomez (reviewer): The hysteresis window seems reasonable; can we expose it as an operator knob?
Priya Raman (author): Exposed as config.slo.enforcer.hysteresis_window_ms with a safe default (1500ms). Documented in docs/infra/README.md.
Lars Ostberg (approver): Verified stress-run results in perf-canary; will approve once CI flakiness is resolved.
CI bot: unit tests initially failed on recovery path (race detected). Author pushed a fix and re-ran CI; subsequent runs passed.
